research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
regression to the mean in half-game splits
counter strategy best and avoid opponents
methodological_questions: Is a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across seasons (split-half or year-to-year reliability)?
Does regression to the mean account for the apparent H2 suppression?
How many team-seasons and possessions are needed to detect a reliable defensive trait?
How sensitive is the estimate to opponent quality, pace, and garbage time?

historical_evidence.finding: First-half reliance on a play type was tested as a predictor of second-half suppression after controlling for H1 PPP and mean reversion. Matched ATT did not survive BH correction (PNR ATT=+0.0313, BH_p=0.0658, WEAK; others NULL). Predictive lift over the mean-reversion baseline was only +0.039 (0.550 vs 0.511). The record concludes that the bulk of H2 suppression is regression to the mean. Sample: n=8873 team-games.

Matchup PPP predictors (equilibrium and actual-mix) had negative R2 on 520 holdout matchup cells (69,876 possessions), while the team-offense mean had R2 +0.1197. A lambda sweep worsened R2 monotonically. Verdict recorded as tool_eval_fail.

Post-hoc matched-pair comparison of teams that abandon versus continue a suppressed play type. At caliper 0.10, group B (n=255 pairs, 242 games) had excess +0.014 with CI [-0.019, +0.046], p=0.386. The record notes B is a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, not a validated successful-adaptation sample, and that the B CIs include 0 at all calipers except 0.15.

Inferred defensive scheme-change labels (523 within-game cells, 440 cross-game pairs) showed change in 61.0% and 67.7% of cases, with near-uniform transition matrices. The record's caveat is that the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.

Descriptive sweep over 870 ordered team pairs found exploitable defensive edges in 33.3% of pairs. The record notes that edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they are not matchup-specific. It draws on an NCAA tournament and ratings dataset, not the NBA per-game files.

Double-suppression stacking (POST_UP then PUTBACK): stacked delta -0.071 vs additive prediction -0.232. The record cites implementation-bug and small-sample limits. It concerns sequential play-type effects, not a team-level defensive trait.

Sequential aftershock effect was positive for 8/8 play types and replicated across all-games and playoff samples (e.g. CUT +0.119, n=21,398 all-games). It concerns offensive sequencing after a successful play, not the defensive H2-H1 trait.
Descriptive BEST/AVOID tier tendencies in H2 trigger possessions across 55 series, 179 players, 25 teams (min 10 possessions). Team AVOID% ranged 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC). No outcome test was run.
Descriptive play-type mix shifts by halftime margin, crunch time and post-run. No inferential tests were run, and the OTHER label is recorded as noisy (PT audit).
Counter play-type matchup specificity: median counter entropy 1.543, reduced by -0.344 when the suppressed play type is known. No inferential test on the entropy values.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using first-half play-type reliance to predict second-half suppression beyond mean reversion
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limitation: LIM:selection_or_regression_to_the_mean (RISK:RTM_SELECTION). Matched ATT did not survive BH; the predictive lift over mean reversion was only +0.039, so the bulk of H2 suppression is regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Post-hoc matched-pair test of adapting versus continuing against a suppressed play type
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable with a post-hoc, reconstructed cohort. The group B CI includes 0 at the primary caliper (p=0.386), and the record flags PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme changes from play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable: LIM:label_or_classification_error (RISK:LABEL_ERROR). The label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution, and near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-level PPP predictive models versus simple team-mean baselines
failed_approaches.why: Both model predictors had negative R2 (equilibrium -0.1981, actual-mix -0.7167) against a team-mean R2 of +0.1197. The record shows the models did not outperform simple means, so the predictive structure was not established.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing additive stacking of two opponent suppression effects
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with LIM:implementation_bug and LIM:small_sample (RISK:IMPLEMENTATION_BUG). The stacked delta (-0.071) differed from the additive prediction (-0.232), but the record gives no clean result.

evidence_establishes: The closest retrieved evidence (SF-APPS-070) shows that apparent second-half suppression in this project's data is largely regression to the mean once first-half performance is controlled for. Any H2-H1 defensive effect must therefore be estimated against a mean-reversion baseline.
Retrieved model and prediction attempts for matchup-level effects (SF-APPA-020, SF-APPS-025) did not produce a validated predictive or adaptation effect.
Label-based defensive measures (SF-APPA-005, SF-APPM-021) carry recorded label-error risk, so an H2-H1 test that relies on inferred play-type labels inherits that risk.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record estimates the split-half or year-to-year reliability of a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change.
No retrieved record analyses NBA team-season defensive H2-H1 effects directly. The retrieved NBA records concern sequencing, adaptation, and play-type labels, while SF-APPA-034 draws on NCAA data.
Whether a stable H2-H1 defensive trait exists after mean-reversion control, and how large it is, remains unknown.
The retrieved summaries are truncated ('read_family for the full text'), so details beyond the excerpts were not reviewed.
own_inferences: The question is answerable in principle from play-by-play data. The 120 team-seasons (about 30 teams × 4 seasons) give limited power for a reliability coefficient, so the test would be underpowered for small true effects.

Because H2-H1 change is strongly mean-reverting (SF-APPS-070), a raw H2-H1 defensive effect will mostly reflect regression to the mean unless the estimate is residualised on H1 performance and opponent strength.
The 2025-26 season is partial before 2026-04-13 and the playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so those data should be excluded or used only after completion.
uncertainties: The retrieval returned no record that tests team-level defensive H2-H1 reliability, so no historical estimate of its magnitude is available.
Half-game splits of NBA team defense may carry very few possessions, which would weaken split-half reliability estimates.
Whether the play-by-play per-game files support clean possession counts for H1 and H2 was not verified in retrieved records.
Rule or pace drift across 2022-23 to 2025-26 could confound season-to-season reliability.
The retrieval did not confirm whether any earlier record tested the question on NBA team defense directly.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence changed the design rather than the proceed decision. SF-APPS-070 showed that H2 suppression is mainly regression to the mean, so the plan must residualise on H1 performance and opponent strength before any reliability claim. SF-APPS-025, SF-APPA-020 and SF-APPA-005 showed that post-hoc cohorts, untuned predictive models and inferred labels are fragile, so the plan uses pre-specified, box-score-and-play-by-play-based measures and excludes partial 2025-26 data. The absence of any direct NBA reliability record means the outcome is genuinely open, and the decision is proceed with changes rather than a plain proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: H2-H1 change is strongly mean-reverting; a raw defensive effect will be dominated by regression to the mean unless residualised on H1 and opponent strength.
120 team-seasons give limited power to detect a reliable trait with a reliability coefficient, especially for small true effects.
Half-game defensive splits may have few possessions, so the split-half reliability of the measure itself is uncertain.
Opponent quality, pace, and garbage-time composition can drive H2-H1 differences independently of defense.
Season-to-season changes in rules, pace, and roster continuity may confound the cross-season reliability estimate.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record directly tests whether a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable trait. The closest work, SF-APPS-070, found the H2 suppression signal largely explained by regression to the mean, with only a weak predictive lift. Other retrieved records (SF-APPA-020, SF-APPS-025, SF-APPA-005) report failed or untestable attempts at related matchup, adaptation, and label-based questions. The question is therefore only partly addressed by prior work, and the reliability question itself remains open.

risks.text: Selecting extreme team-seasons on H2-H1 change inflates apparent reliability through regression to the mean (see SF-APPS-070).
About 120 team-seasons may not support a precise reliability estimate, and power is unknown for realistic effect sizes.
Defensive H2-H1 measures built on half-game splits may have low split-half reliability.
Opponent strength, pace, and garbage time can produce apparent defensive H2-H1 effects.
Play-type labels (e.g. OTHER) are noisy (SF-APPM-021, SF-APPA-005), so label-based defensive measures may be biased.
Partial 2025-26 data and possible season-level drift could bias cross-season reliability.
Scanning many defensive definitions, windows, and splits risks selecting one that appears reliable.
Derived possession and H1/H2 splitting logic from the play-by-play and graph database may contain errors (SF09 limitation).
Post-hoc cohorts (SF-APPS-025) show that placebo-like or noise-driven effects can appear without a validated control.

design.estimand: Year-to-year and split-half reliability (intraclass correlation) of each team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 scoring change, after residualising on opponent H1 PPP and opponent strength.
design.unit: Team-season (defensive team), using regular-season games only for the primary analysis.
design.sample: Complete regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 (about 90 team-seasons, 30 teams each). Playoffs and the partial 2025-26 season are excluded from the primary analysis and reserved as a holdout only after completion.
design.power: Pre-compute the minimum detectable reliability coefficient using simulated possession counts per team-season and a bootstrap over games. Report the power to detect a stated reliability (e.g. ICC ≥ 0.3) before running the test. If power is below 0.8, report the result as underpowered rather than as a rejection.
design.controls: Residualise opponent H2-H1 change on opponent H1 PPP (mean reversion), opponent strength, pace, and garbage-time flags (score margin threshold fixed in advance). Use shrinkage (empirical Bayes) for team effects. Freeze all definitions before any reliability calculation.
design.falsification: Compare the defense effect against a placebo defined on offensive H2-H1 change of the same teams, and against a shuffled-team-label null. A reliable trait claim requires the defensive reliability to exceed the placebo reliability and the shuffled null.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary reliability metric (year-to-year correlation of the residualised shrunk effect). Treat other windows, splits and play-type-specific variants as exploratory with BH correction.
design.decision_rule: Declare a reliable trait only if the primary reliability is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0, exceeds the placebo reliability, and survives the mean-reversion residualisation. If the CI includes 0 at adequate power, report as rejected (adequately powered null). If power is inadequate, report as uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files as of 2026-10-06, regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete; 2025-26 excluded from the primary analysis; play-type labels frozen with the audit version recorded.

how many team-seasons are needed to detect a reliable defensive trait
does regression to the mean or selection of extreme team-seasons inflate apparent reliability

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
